inputs.share_count_basis: Weighted-average diluted shares for H1 FY2026 EPS (6,423.6m: 6,312.2m basic + 111.4m dilutive options/RSUs), interim report note 'Earnings per share'. The 6,677.0m shares in issue at 30 Jun 2026 include ~365m held by the share-scheme trustee (excluded from the EPS denominator) and 53.3m repurchased shares cancelled in July 2026. Held FLAT: SBC is expensed in the flows (charging both would double-count); the USD1.2bn/48-month buyback (RMB582m spent in H1 FY2026) more than funds the flat count.
inputs.cash_composition: 30 Jun 2026, RMB m: cash and equivalents 15,760.8 + term deposits 1,475.4 + wealth management products at FVTPL 18,327.6 (14,948.9 non-current + 3,378.8 current, interim note 15) + treasury investments at amortized cost ~2,100 (residual of the company's stated RMB38.2bn 'cash resources' after the other lines and restricted cash). Restricted cash 500.8 (pledged) excluded. Preferred-share and listed-equity investments at FVTPL (941m) excluded, conservative.
inputs.debt_composition: 30 Jun 2026, RMB m: borrowings 5,174.6 (4,904.3 non-current + 270.3 current) + put option to Kuayue Express non-controlling interests 2,183.0 (committed cash consideration for the remaining Kuayue equity, interim note 'accrued expenses'). Lease liabilities (18,704.3) EXCLUDED because the lease payment is charged inside the flows (treatment B).
inputs.lease_cash_fy0_note: FY2025 principal portion of lease payments 6,873.8 (financing, AR p.5815) + interest expense on lease liabilities 680.8 (AR p.7290). last_fcf = reported_fcf 11,844.6 - SBC 390.9 - finance income 1,096.8 - lease cash 7,554.6 = 2,802.3 (owner FCF margin 1.3%; FY2024 on the same basis was ~5,780 / 3.2%).
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 annual report cash-flow statement add-back 'Share-based payments' RMB390,875k (p.1036); equity-award taxes 0 (no net-share-settlement tax line disclosed). H1 FY2026: 267.6m.
inputs.buyback_note: FY2025 financing activities: no repurchases. H1 FY2026: RMB581.7m (53.3m shares) under the USD1.2bn/48-month program announced May 2026.
inputs.fx_note: CNY/HKD 1.175 (Yahoo CNYHKD=X, 2026-10-22T03:29Z). Parity check: USDHKD 7.8453 / USDCNY 6.6737 = 1.1755, ties to 0.05%. Statements and flows are RMB; the HKEX quote is HKD. Per-share values are computed in RMB and multiplied by 1.175 into HKD; no dual listing exists for a price parity check.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-10-22T03:13:53Z (intraday, HKEX morning session; not a close)
inputs.wacc_rationale: Built in CNY, the currency of the flows: 10y China government bond ~1.8%, China ERP ~6.5%, beta ~1.1 for a capital-intensive logistics operator (CoE ~9%), ~95% equity weight with borrowings at ~2.2% -> ~9% unadjusted. A +2pp governance/related-party premium is added ONCE in the discount rate (11.0%): ~37% of revenue is priced by the controlling shareholder under connected transactions, and the market has demanded a persistent discount (ex-lease EV/EBITDA 3-4x, P/E 13-17x in FY2024-25). The first build at 9.5% tripped the multiples sanity check (implied P/E 34.8x vs 2x the 10yr average 15.4x); per the project's fix priority (mid-cycle FCF not applicable -- FY2025 owner FCF is below FY2024, so the base is not peak; WACC premium next) the premium was applied as the single fix pass. The same 11.0% is used in all three scenarios; operating risk (JD dependency, on-demand delivery losses, margin compression) is carried in the scenario flows and weights, not in per-scenario WACC differences.
inputs.lease_treatment: (B) Leases as operating cost. The full lease payment (principal + interest on lease liabilities, both read off the cash-flow statement / finance-cost note) is charged inside EBIT via lease_cost_pct_path (3.48% of revenue FY2025, 3.15% H1 FY2026); lease liabilities (RMB18.7bn) are EXCLUDED from net debt; D&A for cash-tax EBIT is ex right-of-use depreciation (FY2025 total D&A 12,986 less ROU depreciation ~7,600 = ~5,390 = 2.5% of revenue; H1 FY2026 2.4%). Non-IFRS EBITDA margins (post-IFRS-16, pre-lease) are the ebitda_margin_path anchor.
inputs.nci_treatment: NCI deducted once in the equity bridge at book (RMB1,106.7m at 30 Jun 2026, down from 5,104.4m after the Deppon privatisation); flows are modelled on a consolidated basis. The committed Kuayue put-option consideration (2,183.0m) is treated as debt, not NCI.
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF component DCF (operating company, non-US, material leases, NCI, dual currency: owner-fcf.md + owner-fcf-adaptations.md a/b/c/d/f). First valuation of this ticker; no memory entry. Interest/finance income (RMB1,096.8m FY2025) is stripped from the flows because the matching assets (RMB37.7bn cash, deposits and wealth-management products) are added in the bridge; net cash is ~11x the owner-FCF base. FY0 = FY2025 (Dec year-end); Y1 = FY2026, of which H1 is reported (revenue +26.5%, non-IFRS EBITDA margin 8.8%). Related-party revenue from JD Group is ~37% of FY2025 revenue and rising (on-demand delivery business acquired from JD Group Oct 2025). Historical comparability is distorted by consolidation of Deppon (2022), Kuayue (to 100% in 2025) and JD's on-demand delivery business (Oct 2025). The price is an intraday HKEX print and should be replaced at the next regular close. Market context at the valuation price: equity ~RMB53.5bn, ex-lease EV ~RMB24bn, ~1.9x FY2025 EBITDA less lease cash -- the stock has traded at 2-5x on this basis since 2022, so most of the modelled upside is a re-rating the market has never granted; see valuation_philosophy.

equity_bridge.note: 30 Jun 2026 interim balance sheet; residual Deppon and other subsidiary minorities after the March 2026 Deppon buyout

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: judgment: revenue 3yr CAGR (16.5%, FY2022-25) haircut for the M&A/consolidation component (Deppon, Kuayue, on-demand delivery); 10% is the base-case organic rate for FY2027-28 (Y2-Y3)
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 3yr CAGR 5.5% vs revenue 16.5%: equity growth is suppressed by NCI buyouts (Kuayue, Deppon) charged directly to equity and by the loss years, not by weak retention. EPS CAGRs are undefined (FY2022 EPS -0.23, FY2020 -1.05). Owner-FCF CAGRs are undefined on a 3/5-year basis (FY2022 owner FCF ~-0.1bn after lease cash) and volatile on a 2-year basis (FY2023 ~0.8bn, FY2024 ~5.8bn, FY2025 ~2.8bn): working-capital swings dominate a 1-3% margin.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF series (reported FCF - SBC - finance income - lease principal - lease interest), RMB m: FY2022 ~-144, FY2023 ~788, FY2024 ~5,780, FY2025 2,802. Reported FCF CAGR FY2022-25 of 11.8% is flattered by lease principal sitting in financing (RMB6.2-7.4bn/yr).

base.growth_rationale: FY2026 +23%: H1 +26.5% reported, H2 ~+20% as the on-demand delivery business (consolidated 31 Oct 2025) enters the base in Nov-Dec; FY2027-28 10-12% as external ISC (+11-14%) and on-demand growth continue on an organic base; decelerating to 3% by FY2035 as China logistics matures.
base.margin_rationale: Non-IFRS EBITDA margin 11.1% FY2024, 9.5% FY2025, 8.8% H1 FY2026 (on-demand scale-up, energy costs). FY2026 8.9%, then re-expansion of ~0.3pp/yr toward 10.5% as on-demand losses narrow and automation (LangzuTech, Metabrain) lowers unit cost -- still below the FY2024 peak. Lease cost 3.3% -> 3.2%, D&A ex-ROU 2.4%, capex 2.9% -> 2.7% (FY2025 3.2%, H1 FY2026 2.5%).
base.tax_rationale: Cash tax FY2025 RMB910m on pre-tax 7.3bn = 12.4% (preferential rates, loss carryforwards); ramps to 20% by Y8 as carryforwards are used and the 25% statutory rate bites on more subsidiaries.
base.wc_rationale: Receivables (RMB22bn, ~10% of revenue) grow with external ISC and on-demand revenue; working capital consumed ~2.2bn on 34bn of revenue growth in FY2025 (-6%) and ~0.2bn on 16bn in FY2024 (-1%); -3% capture on the revenue change.
base.wacc_note: 11.0% = ~9% CNY CoE/WACC + 2pp governance/related-party premium, applied once (see inputs.wacc_rationale and sanity_fix).

scenario_narratives.base: JD Group volumes keep growing mid-single digits and external integrated-supply-chain revenue compounds 10-14% as brand customers (FMCG, appliances, autos, luxury) outsource warehousing; on-demand delivery scales to break-even by FY2028 and the FY2025/H1 FY2026 margin trough proves cyclical, with non-IFRS EBITDA margin re-expanding ~0.3pp a year to 10.5% -- still below FY2024's 11.1%. Lease and capex intensity drift down slightly as the Asia No.1 park network matures. Owner-FCF margin rises from ~1.5% to ~3.4% by FY2035, in line with the FY2024 high-water mark. Gordon at 11%/2.5% binds (12.1x) below the 15x cap.
scenario_narratives.bull: Automation (LangzuTech GTP, Metabrain) and the consolidated freight platform (Deppon + Kuayue at 100%) deliver the structural cost advantage management claims: EBITDA margin returns to 11% by FY2030 and 12% by FY2035; on-demand delivery becomes a profitable last-mile density engine rather than a subsidy sink; JoyExpress and overseas warehousing add a second growth leg so revenue growth stays double-digit through FY2029; the buyback is sustained. Requires several independent things to go right, hence the 20% weight.
scenario_narratives.bear: JD.com's e-commerce growth slows and intercompany pricing is renegotiated in the parent's favour; on-demand delivery stays loss-making against Meituan/Alibaba and gig-worker social-insurance rules lift labour cost (the largest cost line, ~RMB80bn); the Tongda network and SF cap external pricing so the EBITDA margin settles at 8.4-8.8% and never recovers FY2024 levels; lease and capex intensity stay at FY2025 levels; cash tax normalises faster. Growth fades to 2.5% by FY2033. The terminal cap is 12x in this scenario; owner-FCF margin stays ~1.5%.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised to 30% from the 15% default: ~37% of revenue (and rising) is from the controlling shareholder under connected-transaction pricing, the on-demand delivery pivot is unproven and subsidy-dependent, and margins have compressed for two consecutive periods. Bull cut to 20% because it needs margin re-expansion, on-demand profitability and overseas traction to all land. Base 50%.

valuation_philosophy.summary: A thin-margin, capital-intensive logistics network with a captive anchor customer and RMB30bn of net cash. Value is a function of whether the FY2025-26 EBITDA margin compression is a trough or the new normal, and of what multiple a minority holder can expect for cash flows whose pricing is set by the controlling shareholder. The DCF charges leases as an operating cost (treatment B), strips finance income and adds the cash pile in the bridge, expenses SBC (immaterial here) and holds the count flat. Most of the modelled upside versus the market price is a re-rating the stock has not been granted since 2022 (ex-lease EV/EBITDA has sat at ~2-5x); the required-return table is the honest reading of what today's price implies.
key_risks_to_valuation: Related-party concentration: ~37% of revenue from JD Group under connected-transaction pricing; a renegotiation or JD GMV slowdown hits the largest revenue line directly
Margin trajectory: non-IFRS EBITDA margin 11.1% -> 9.5% -> 8.8%; the base case assumes recovery to 10.5%, which has not yet started
On-demand delivery: capital- and subsidy-intensive entry against Meituan/Alibaba; JD's new-business segment lost RMB46.6bn in 2025
Labour regulation: gig-worker social insurance on ~540k delivery personnel is the largest cost line
Cash pile quality: RMB18.3bn of 'cash resources' are wealth-management products at FVTPL; treated as cash-like at book
Owner-FCF margin is 1-3%, so small working-capital swings move the FCF base materially
Low historical multiple: the market has never paid more than ~5x ex-lease EV/EBITDA since 2022; the Gordon terminal implies a re-rating

sanity_fix.fix_applied: WACC premium: 9.5% -> 11.0% in all scenarios (+2pp governance/related-party premium charged once in the discount rate). Mid-cycle FCF fix judged not applicable: the FY2025 owner-FCF base (RMB2.8bn, 1.3% margin) is below FY2024 (RMB5.8bn, 3.2%), so the base year is not a peak; growth and exit-multiple caps left unchanged (base implied terminal EV/EBITDA 4.7x at 9.5% was already inside the stock's own 3-5x range).
sanity_fix.note: sanity_check.py is known to apply fx_rate in the wrong direction on dual-currency tickers (see memory: sanity-check-fx-rate-direction-systemic-bug); on a CNY basis the first-pass implied P/E was ~28x on SBC-adjusted FY2025 EPS, which would not have tripped the 2x rule. The premium is nonetheless defensible on its own terms and is kept.
